parts.note: an inn is a public house with a bar, so bar stands for inn
an ovation is a burst of applause, public acclaim

explanation.surface: A pub's bar earns applause for trying something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a verb meaning forbid, but it is a noun: a pub, INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty or new invention is a fresh creation, something novel.

parts.note: if is a conjunction joining clauses
or is another joining conjunction

explanation.surface: The joining words a Welshman uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjunctions' gives two pieces, IF and OR. Ifor is a Welsh man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifor is a traditional Welsh forename, so it names a man from Wales.

annotationWithheld.why: Oily bairn of rank: an anagram of OILY BAIRN with no anagram indicator in the clue (1960s Times style); no clue word can signal the rearrangement

clue.text: Plea of old ladies wishing to cross

definitions.text: Plea of old ladies wishing to cross

parts.words: Plea of old ladies wishing to cross
parts.note: the cross is the mark on a ballot paper, and the ladies are the suffragettes of a century ago

explanation.surface: Elderly women asking for help crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of elderly women at a kerb; the crossing is the X a voter marks, and the plea is the suffragette slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffragette campaign's slogan, demanding the right of women to mark a ballot paper.

definitions.meaning: comparative of tangy, sharper in taste
the Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: A fortified wine with more flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of tangy, more sharply flavoured, and the Moroccan seaport opposite Gibraltar.

clue.text: So Italian river rises on account of one small beast

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the two words turn round together

parts.note: taken as written
the Po is Italy's longest river
a sum is a reckoning or account

explanation.surface: An Italian river climbs, and so a small animal appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns SO PO upwards to give OPOS; add SUM for account. 'on' only links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a small American marsupial, one little animal.

parts.note: a playing card with a single pip, and in tennis the unreturnable serves that top-seeded players send down

explanation.surface: Pips are taken out of fruit seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Pips and seeds suggest fruit; here the pips are card symbols, and the seeds are seeded tennis players, whose serves can be winners outright.
explanation.definitionFit: The top card of each suit carries one pip, and an unreturned tennis serve has the same name, a typical weapon of seeded players.

parts.note: a brittle snack eaten at a break, and one that snaps when bitten

explanation.surface: A snack to eat at break time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is both a pause for a snack and what a brittle snack does when bitten.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin fried potato slice is a small snack that snaps easily, a morsel for a break.

clue.text: South Africa genus of lepidoptera in the Aegean

indicators.note: genus of lepidoptera means a race of moths, so the insect word comes first and the kind follows it

parts.note: A is a common abbreviation for Africa
moths belong to the insect order Lepidoptera
a race is a kind or genus of creature

explanation.surface: A species of butterfly from South Africa found in the Aegean.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'genus of lepidoptera' but the pieces go MOTH then RACE, a race of moths. Samothrace is a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samothrace is a Greek island in the north Aegean, so a place found in that sea.

parts.note: the climbers are hop vines grown up supports; the jumpers are the other sense of hop

explanation.surface: Something for novice climbers, not for jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green climbers' suggests beginner mountaineers; they are hop plants, and 'not jumpers' warns off the leaping sense of hop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall stakes in a hop garden support the climbing bines of the plant used to flavour beer.

parts.note: read not as mope about but as the path a moon traces round its planet

explanation.surface: Someone is mooning about idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon around' is an idiom for drifting about aimlessly; read literally, it asks for the circling path of a moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite's circuit round a planet is its path in space, the course a moon travels.

annotationWithheld.why: New word for oil gnomes: an anagram of OIL GNOMES with no anagram indicator in the clue (1960s Times style); 'New' is the definition, so it cannot also signal the rearrangement

parts.note: not thoughtful periodicals but ones printed on shiny paper that reflects light

explanation.surface: Periodicals that make you think deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' suggests thoughtful; the magazines reflect light from their shiny paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiny-papered periodicals, especially fashion ones, are called this from their lustrous pages.

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations

explanation.surface: A Dickens character expecting something receives a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expectant' points to Great Expectations, whose hero is Pip; add IT. A pipit is a small brown songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small songbird of open country, so it is a kind of bird.

parts.note: a mermaid's tail is covered in scales, so a dummy of her would be scaly; also a replica built to exact proportions

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's dummy shaped like a mermaid with a good figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A mermaid has a scaly tail, so her mannequin is a model with scales; the phrase also means a reduced replica in true proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica reduced in size but kept in exact proportion, here also a figure covered in fish scales.

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to bargain over price
read as one who chaffs, a teasing banterer

explanation.surface: Bargaining with a comedian over the fee.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for bargaining, and also, read as one who chaffs, a banterer or joker.

clue.text: Sailor in alarm, wrecked on the coast

indicators.note: the sailor's letters are placed inside the scrambled word
a wrecked thing is smashed apart, so the letters of alarm are rearranged

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman in a panic after shipwreck on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' is the usual AB, and 'wrecked on the coast' looks like a shipwreck but splits: 'wrecked' scrambles, and 'on the' just links to the definition, the south-west coast of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malabar Coast is the long south-western seaboard of India, a stretch of shore.

clue.text: Osteopath who met his Water loo ?

definitions.text: Osteopath who met his Water loo ?

parts.words: Osteopath who met his Water loo ?
parts.note: an osteopath sets bones apart, and the man who met his Waterloo was the French emperor

explanation.surface: A bone doctor who suffered a final defeat, with a lavatory joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname sounds like 'bone apart', fitting an osteopath, and Waterloo, split as water loo, was Napoleon's defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor's surname, the man defeated at Waterloo, here heard as bone apart for a bone specialist.

clue.text: Made to strike by being held down

definitions.text: Made to strike by being held down

parts.words: Made to strike by being held down
parts.note: a gardening sense: a shoot pegged into the soil until it strikes, or takes root

explanation.surface: Workers forced to go on strike after being oppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action; in gardening a cutting strikes when it roots, and a stem pegged down into soil to root is propagated this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Propagating a plant by pegging a stem into the soil until it roots is the gardener's technique of this name.

parts.note: not finding an apartment but letting the air out of a tyre

explanation.surface: Advice on renting an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flat' suggests an apartment; it is a flat tyre, got by letting the air out.
explanation.definitionFit: To let air out of something, as a tyre, until it collapses, which is how a tyre goes flat.

parts.note: the full title of the brotherhood is the Free and Accepted Masons

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the free and the welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase stops one word short of the order's full name, Free and Accepted Masons; the adjective for that brotherhood is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things belonging to the Freemasons, whose formal title includes Free and Accepted.

clue.text: Score of Patience, played without a score

definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience opens with twenty lovesick young women, a score being twenty
in cricket, an over in which the batsman scores no runs

explanation.surface: The music of an opera, performed without the sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty lovesick young women who form the chorus in the opera Patience, and cricket overs bowled without a run conceded.

definitions.meaning: the Scottish explorer of the Niger was ... Park, so Park is a surname wanting its forename
St ..., also called Kentigern, is the patron saint of Glasgow

explanation.surface: A park designed in a saintly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the explorer Park, and the name borne by Glasgow's patron saint.

definitions.meaning: quick and agile on one's feet
a Lyons tea-shop waitress in Britain was called a ...

explanation.surface: A quick-footed waitress, even if a little cold.
explanation.definitionFit: It means quick on the feet, sharply cold, and was the name for a waitress in the Lyons tea-shop chain in Britain.

clue.text: So like a blonde, past all correction!

definitions.text: So like a blonde, past all correction

parts.words: So like a blonde, past all correction
parts.note: read as a likeness of a light-haired person, and as a clean final draft with every correction done

explanation.surface: Exclaiming that someone resembles a blonde and is quite incorrigible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' means blonde, so a likeness of a blonde is a fair copy; the phrase also means a neat document written out once corrections are complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean transcript made after all amendments are finished, here also a likeness of a light-haired person.

clue.text: Vessel by which the artist returned beside the waters of Eden

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: returned means the artist's letters are turned back

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A cup an artist brought back from Paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns RA into AR. 'the waters of Eden' are not Paradise but the River Eden, on which the Fife town of Cupar stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupar is a market town in Fife, Scotland, standing on the River Eden.

clue.text: To you upset and landed in the river

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the words are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Distressed, you came ashore in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TO YE upwards into EYOT. 'landed' is not a verb here: it means land, ground, sitting in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot, or ait, is a small island in a river, a piece of land in the stream.

annotationWithheld.why: Disapprove of Peter Cade: an anagram of PETER CADE with no anagram indicator in the clue (1960s Times style); no clue word can signal the rearrangement

clue.text: Ward off a man of staves

definitions.meaning: to fend off a blow, as in fencing
Staves are the lines music is written on

explanation.surface: Fending off a man armed with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect a blow, and the surname of the composer Hubert Parry, a man whose work is written on musical staves.

definitions.meaning: ley farming rotates fields between crops and temporary grass

explanation.surface: A college that teaches pasture farming.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leys is a Cambridge school, and leys are fields sown with grass for a few years in crop rotation.

parts.note: Davy Jones rules the ocean bed, so his wife lives in the sea; her tempter, like Eve's, would be a snake, here a marine monster

explanation.surface: Who might lead a Mrs Jones astray?
explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones is sailors' slang for the spirit of the sea bed; Eve was tempted by a serpent, so his wife's tempter would be a serpent of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary monster of the ocean, shaped like a giant snake, the tempter of Eden moved to the deep.
